items.q: Is Mastercard Agent Pay the same as AP2?
items.a: No. AP2 is an open mandate protocol that Google launched and contributed to the FIDO Alliance in 2026-04; Agent Pay is Mastercard's proprietary card-network program. They connect only through Verifiable Intent, which uses the same four mandate type strings as AP2 v0.2 on its main branch.

items.q: Is a Mastercard agentic token the same as a Visa agentic token?
items.a: No. The words are shared but the products are separate: Mastercard Agentic Tokens belong to Agent Pay, and Visa's agentic network tokens belong to Visa Intelligent Commerce.

items.q: Is Agent Pay live at scale?
items.a: Mastercard has enabled issuers at network level in several regions, but the transactions it names are pilots, controlled trials or first transactions, and it publishes no volume data.

items.q: Are agentic tokens issued by MDES?
items.a: Mastercard's Agent Pay developer page, as read on 2026-10-21, calls Agent Pay a Remote Commerce Tokenization Program and lists network tokenization through MDES (Mastercard Digital Enablement Service) among its technologies. Since 2026-08-05 the MDES Customer Service API also lets issuers enabled for Agent Pay set token-level spend limits.

items.q: Is DTVC a kind of agentic token?
items.a: No. A DTVC is a one-time security code issued with a Mastercard Virtual Card Token for guest checkouts. Mastercard pages expand it both as Validation Code and as Verification Code.

items.q: Which tag does a Mastercard agent put in Signature-Input?
items.a: Mastercard's Level 1 guide gives Agent-pay-auth; its testing glossary writes agent-pay-auth. The browse and pay tags agent-browser-auth and agent-payer-auth are Visa's.

items.q: Where is the Mastercard key directory?
items.a: Unknown publicly. The only host in Mastercard's example, agentpay-key-directory.mastercard.com, did not resolve on 2026-10-11 or on 2026-10-21. Cloudflare said in 2025-10 that each network will host its own directory but names no Mastercard URL.

items.q: Does a merchant need new code to accept Agent Pay?
items.a: Not at Level 1. The agent types the token into the existing card form and the token looks like a card number; signature checks can run at the CDN. PCI scope does not change.

items.q: Is the Mastercard Agent Toolkit a payments SDK?
items.a: No. It is an MCP server and library that reads Mastercard documentation and API specifications, and it makes no payment calls. No public SDK or sandbox for card Agent Pay was found as of 2026-10-21; on 2026-10-20 Mastercard opened Agent Pay for Machines Early Access with buyer- and seller-side APIs, a toolkit and a sandbox.

items.q: Does Mastercard say AP4M is compatible with MPP?
items.a: Not in its own words. In Mastercard's 2026-06-10 AP4M release, Tempo says it is working with Mastercard on Machine Payments Protocol compatibility. Mastercard's own 2026-10-20 brief says AP4M builds on x402 and names no MPP.

items.q: What happens in a dispute over an agent purchase?
items.a: Standard chargeback rights apply. No agent-specific reason code or liability shift is published: Mastercard's public rules point participants to Mastercard Agent Pay Program Standards, which are not public, so any agent-specific dispute terms cannot be checked. Verifiable Intent provides evidence but assigns no liability.

items.q: Which version of Verifiable Intent should I code against?
items.a: The 0.1 label covers two sets of names. Tag v0.1.0 (2026-03-05) uses names such as payment.amount; main after 2026-04-20 uses mandate.payment.amount_range and .1 suffixes. This atlas follows main.
